articleTitle: 100 kHz, 2 KW boost ZVT-PWM converter for power factor correction
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1993 Power Electronics Congress (Congreso Internacional de Electronica de Polentia)
abstract: Power factor correction has become an important topic in power electronics. The classical boost single-phase power factor correction (PFC) schemes have a serious problem. While running under CCM operation, the diode reverse recovery problem causes significant losses when the output voltage is quite high. This not only decreases the total efficiency, but also creates thermal and noise problems. To solve this problem, the zero-voltage transition (ZVT) technique has been developed which allows the use of IGBT, reducing the switching loss and achieve low conduction loss. A prototype circuit has been built and tested to verify this new technique.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An improved three phase diode rectifier with input power factor correction
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1993 Power Electronics Congress (Congreso Internacional de Electronica de Polentia)
abstract: A new approach to improve power factor and reduce harmonics generated by a three phase diode rectifier is proposed. The proposed approach is passive and consists of a novel interconnection of a star/delta transformer between the AC and DC sides of the diode rectifier topology. This novel interconnection is shown to generate a circulating third harmonic current between the AC and DC side of the rectifier bridge. The circulating third harmonic current is then shown to drastically improve the performance of the diode rectifier type interface. The resulting point current is near sinusoidal in shape with significant reduction in line current harmonics. Experimental results from a 6 kW laboratory prototype are detailed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A practical implementation of a two fully regulated outputs converter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1993 Power Electronics Congress (Congreso Internacional de Electronica de Polentia)
abstract: The authors describe a prototype developed to achieve a second fully regulated output added to a forward zero current switched quasi resonant converter (ZCS-QRC) and at the same time, to describe the advantages of this base topology in this kind of application. In addition, circuit operation of the secondary resonance forward converter is explained. Voltage and current waveforms is analyzed as functions of times and input/output conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Modeling the modulated-frequency boost AC-DC preregulator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1993 Power Electronics Congress (Congreso Internacional de Electronica de Polentia)
abstract: Small-signal models for modulated-frequency boost AC-DC preregulators using the current injected equivalent circuit approach are presented. Implementations with and without input voltage feedforward are analyzed, considering three different types of load (resistive, constant power and constant current). Correlated transfer functions are obtained. The simulated results agree with predicted model-results, validating the transfer functions to be used in control loop design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of microcontrollers to control HVDC converters
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1993 Power Electronics Congress (Congreso Internacional de Electronica de Polentia)
abstract: The author presents the design of the hardware and software of the AC/DC converter controllers for an HVDC transmission system. The structure of the converter controllers is based on a 16-b microcontroller. The microcontroller includes the facilities needed to support fast real-time control in a single chip. The main functions included in the terminal controllers are the control of the firing instants of the bridge valves, the control of the transformer tap changer, and the monitoring of the signals needed for the control and study of the HVDC transmission system. One of the special features of this controller is that, with the use of the high-speed input/output system of the microcontroller, the precision to detect input pulses and to output thyristor firing signals is not affected by the corresponding latency in the response of the CPU to the interrupts. This work contains the details of the design of the AC and DC voltage and current transducers, the thyristor conducting state detectors, the thyristor gating circuits, the microcontroller expansion interface, and the software of the terminal controllers. This design was tested on an HVDC transmission system model. Experimental results are also presented here.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of a two stage, 1 kW AC/DC power factor pre-regulator, using the FB-ZVS-PWM topology
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1993 Power Electronics Congress (Congreso Internacional de Electronica de Polentia)
abstract: The authors present the results of the implementation of a two stage AC/DC pre-regulator, using a boost converter (as a power factor corrector), and a full bridge zero voltage switched-PWM converter, in order to improve the dynamic features of the DC bus, working as well as a battery charger within the scheme of distributed power supply in which it will be used.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Educational workbench for testing the control techniques of switched DC/DC convertors
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1993 Power Electronics Congress (Congreso Internacional de Electronica de Polentia)
abstract: In this paper an educational workbench is presented. Its purpose is to develop several practice exercises about DC-to-DC converter control. This system allows one to analyze most of control techniques of nonresonant switched converters. Modular and trainer-oriented design and intrinsic security have been the most important points during the workbench development time. In order to provide an ideal introductory power converter course. However, some advanced topics (complete design, static and dynamic modelling etc.) are also possible with this system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of AC drives with position and speed dynamic control using DSP
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1993 Power Electronics Congress (Congreso Internacional de Electronica de Polentia)
abstract: A field orientation scheme for current fed induction motor drives is presented. The first part of this work gives a short introduction about principles of field orientation. After this the authors describe the used hardware. The control is implemented on a TMS320C30 DSP with new digital signal processors with which it is possible reduce the sampling time for the control loop and use floating point arithmetic. At last, some experimental results are shown where the prototype performances are shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of a deceleration system for unwinding machine using a microcontroller
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1993 Power Electronics Congress (Congreso Internacional de Electronica de Polentia)
abstract: The development of an automatic deceleration system for a winding machine in a siderurgy factory is shown in this paper. The system not only supplies the angular speed reference, but a bobbin diameter measurement as well; it must be able to recognize emergency stop signals and supply certain parameters to process supervision. The specifications required to control the system point to digital technics as the better solution to perform DC control; in this case, a microcontroller was used. This work has been financed by Asturias (SPAIN) siderurgy enterprise ENSIDESA.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A parallel inverter for energy saving
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1993 Power Electronics Congress (Congreso Internacional de Electronica de Polentia)
abstract: A new parallel inverter was designed with a current source model to equilibrate the consumption and compensate the capacitive energy. It uses the oriented field theory in active and reactive power regulation, and the sliding method in the power poles control. The result is an energy transference between AC and DC in both ways without harmonics. The same converter provides connection to photovoltaic cells. A 30-kVA prototype unit is finished.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Current-fed self-controlled synchronous machine simulation tools and elements for optimal operating conditions
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1993 Power Electronics Congress (Congreso Internacional de Electronica de Polentia)
abstract: The aim of this work is to present and justify the set of models of the current-fed self-controlled synchronous machine (SCSM) the authors have developed how to optimize the control of such a complex system. Dynamic and steady state comparative results about the currents, the voltages-EMF phase shift, the thyristor blocking time, the average torque/DC link current ratio are given. A thyristor blocking time control strategy, implemented and tested in digital simulation to obtain the maximum available torque for each value of supply current by closed loop control of the reverse voltage application time of the SCRs, is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A high frequency, high performance range of power supplies using surface mount technology (SMT)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1993 Power Electronics Congress (Congreso Internacional de Electronica de Polentia)
abstract: A In a large number of industrial electronic applications, several DC voltage values are needed. For this purpose, a range of power supplies is designed and built. All of them have the same board and the same components except for power transformer, decreasing production costs. The right design of inductive elements and the use of high frequency, low cost and low volume power supplies. Full protection, very careful control design and the use of a good voltage reference provide a high performance range of power supplies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Nonlinear continuous time control of a bidirectional boost converter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1993 Power Electronics Congress (Congreso Internacional de Electronica de Polentia)
abstract: Nonlinear control of a bidirectional boost converter suitable for large-signal applications is presented. The converter is accurately modeled as a second order bilinear system and the conditions established for local stability. The nonlinear control law is implemented by means of one analog divider, standard operational amplifiers and a pulse-width modulator. As a result, the output variable follows proportionally the reference signal, thus allowing the obtention of different types of power waveforms in the converter output.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electronic circuit for automatic transfer of a distribution node
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1993 Power Electronics Congress (Congreso Internacional de Electronica de Polentia)
abstract: This paper shows the design of an electronic prototype, which senses the values for alternating voltage in two different electric distribution systems. The device connects the load to its normal source if the voltage levels are within a permissible range, in order cases the load is connected to an alternate source. The inverse action is accomplished automatically when the voltage returns to its normal value. The main components of the device are: operational amplifiers, timers, logical gates and triacs which gives a low cost alternative. The prototype also has a manual operation stage which permits one to maneuver in permanent fault conditions or when it is necessary to undertake maintenance work.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An object-oriented tool for design of power electronic circuits using personal computers
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1993 Power Electronics Congress (Congreso Internacional de Electronica de Polentia)
abstract: This paper presents the use of an object-oriented environment for design, analysis and teaching of power electronic circuits which may be implemented in tutorial sessions. The main advantages of this approach are: its ease of use, its interactive nature and user-friendliness. The paper describes part of an on-going research project on the design of software tools for power electronic circuits for PC platforms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: 2 kW series resonant converter for CO/sub 2/ gas discharge laser
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1993 Power Electronics Congress (Congreso Internacional de Electronica de Polentia)
abstract: The paper describes the conception and design of a high voltage power supply. Basically it is composed of a series resonant converter operating in continuous conduction mode and a high voltage transformer which feeds high voltage stack rectifiers diodes without a smoothing filter. The suggested converter is very applicable to CO/sub 2/ laser excitation. The inverter works in a continuous or pulsed way with an output power of 2 kW. The power regulation is performed by frequency variation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Guide for installation of 50-300 kVA uninterruptible power systems (UPS)
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1993 Power Electronics Congress (Congreso Internacional de Electronica de Polentia)
abstract: The authors discuss a one module UPS (uninterruptible power system) installation standard which covers the range from 50 to 300 kVA. Special attention has been paid to mechanical requirements, security and services of the rooms dedicated to the UPS and battery, refrigeration, electromagnetic interference, grounding system, differential switch protections, mechanical by-pass, impulse protections and harmonic current filters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effect of harmonic distortion of the supply voltage on the optimum gating angle of a TCR-type compensator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1993 Power Electronics Congress (Congreso Internacional de Electronica de Polentia)
abstract: The authors examine the effect of harmonic distortion of the supply voltage on the optimum gating angle of a thyristor-controlled reactor-type compensator (TCR) and hence its influence on the power factor (PF) correction. The values of optimum PF are compared with those calculated using conventional formulae (which assume that the voltage waveform is purely sinusoidal). The formulae have been simplified by assuming that the switching intervals of the TCR are not affected by the distortion of the voltage supply. This assumption allows one to proceed by considering only one control parameter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Practical design of forward ZCS-QRC converter
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1993 Power Electronics Congress (Congreso Internacional de Electronica de Polentia)
abstract: The authors present the design and analysis of a switch mode power supply employing a forward zero-current switched quasi-resonant converter (ZCS-QRC). The main focus will practical design considerations. For this, the authors introduce some simple and practical equations, which make the design task for these types of converters easier.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Study of the impact of domestic apparatus on distribution lines in Mexico
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1993 Power Electronics Congress (Congreso Internacional de Electronica de Polentia)

articleTitle: Tutorial system as an element in the improvement of power electronic education
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1993 Power Electronics Congress (Congreso Internacional de Electronica de Polentia)
abstract: The paper shows the work done with some advanced students of electronics within the degree of physics. The work has been proposed by a tutor-teacher to develop electronic devices for power applications. As a result of this activity, the authors have obtained some electronic prototypes to use in power filtering. Good results were obtained both in educational and technological areas. Furthermore, this activity has been an example of close collaboration between the University and a private enterprise.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of a forward ZCS-ORC for a distributed power supply system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1993 Power Electronics Congress (Congreso Internacional de Electronica de Polentia)
abstract: This paper deals with the design of a 25 watts Zero Current Switching Quasi-Resonant Converter (ZCS-QRC) employing the forward topology to be used in a distributed power supply system. The resumed specifications for the protype are: input 48 V/spl plusmn/10%, output: 5 V and 5 A, topology: forward ZCS-QRC (full wave mode operation), communication frequency: 500-700 kHz and efficiency: 76 % (worst case conditions). The paper also presents experimental and simulation results obtained with the prototype, as well as the effect of load and input voltage variations in the prototype efficiency and frequency excursions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simplification of switched reluctance motor drives for commercial applications
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1993 Power Electronics Congress (Congreso Internacional de Electronica de Polentia)
abstract: The authors review the SRM (switched reluctance motor) drive technology. They present some of the simplified technology which has been developed in the lab and elsewhere. The emphasis is on elimination of discrete rotor position sensors and discrete current sensors. The theoretical apsects of the different methods of position sensing and the relevant experimental results are also presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Future trends in power factor correction in power systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the 1993 Power Electronics Congress (Congreso Internacional de Electronica de Polentia)
abstract: A summary of the state of the art in power factor correction in power supply systems (general philosophy, properties, control strategies and power topologies) has been given in the first part of this paper. In the second part, a brief analysis of the proposed topologies (soft-switching and precise output-voltage regulation topologies) is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
